The Passive: The Present Continuous and Present Perfect Tenses

You use the Present Continuous to talk about an action that is happening at the time of speaking. The action or event is in progress.
His parents are not allowing him to go back to preschool for a day or two.

You use the Present Perfect to talk about a finished action or event with present consequences. There is a connection between what happened in the past and the present.
His parents have just brought Timmy home from the hospital.
You often choose the passive form when you want to talk about an action but are not so interested in saying who or what does/did it. Passives without agents (the doers) are common in storytelling.
Look at the chart below for the structure of the passive voice.

You use reported speech (indirect speech) when you are saying (reporting) what other people said.
This style of writing is common in storytelling. It allows the writer to share dialogue with the reader without always using quotation marks.

When you tell people what someone has said you generally make the verb tense 'more in the past' since we are reporting the information at a later time. You need to change the verb to the next past form.

You have to change the pronoun if you are reporting what someone else said. Compare these two sentences. In each case the person actually said "I don't want to go."

• I said, “I don't want to go.” > I said I didn't want to go.
  • Bill said, “I don't want to go.” > Bill said he didn't want to go.
When you want to report questions asked, the subject normally comes before the verb. When the question is a yes/no questions, you use if or whether to report it.

Direct: “Can you hide me in a package of peanuts?” he asked his wife.
Indirect: He asked if his wife could hide him in a package of peanuts.

images.text:
Timmy has just been brought home from the hospital. His arm has been broken in an accident. He isn't being allowed to go back to preschool for a day or two.

Timmy is being told a story by his grandmother. He is being rocked in the big chair that has been brought into his room. His grandmother hopes he'll relax and fall asleep. She begins ...

Mr. Tortoise had a good friend, Vulture. Vulture often visited Tortoise. Tortoise said that he was sad because he had never been able to visit Vulture. Tortoise said that because he had no wings and couldn't fly it was impossible.

One day Tortoise had an idea. He asked if his wife could hide him in a package of peanuts. He said that she should tell Vulture the package was for him. He said she should tell Vulture to take it home.

Mrs. Tortoise did this, and Vulture happily secured the package in his beak. While Vulture was soaring home, he heard a voice that said it was his friend, Tortoise. The voice continued, saying that he had come to visit.

Vulture was so surprised to hear a voice coming from the package that he dropped it.The package plummeted down to earth, with Tortoise in it. When it hit the ground, Tortoise's shell broke into pieces.That is how Tortoise got all those cracks in his shell.

Now Timmy has been put into his bed. He's being tucked in tight! He's fast asleep. Shhhh.
